claims.text: A mage who rewrites the Pattern for good in a way reality rejects, such as with some cybernetic changes, carries Paradox that never drains away and worsens every backlash.
Prime cannot remove it; it fades only if the mage undoes the cause or the Consensus comes to accept the change as normal.

title: The upheavals before the Reckoning
summary: Blows that reshaped the Awakened world around 1997 to 1999.

claims.text: Doissetep, in the Umbral reflection of Mars within the Shard Realm of Forces, exploded when it fell to attackers; Porthos Fitz-Empress contained the worst of the blast.
After Doissetep fell, the Digital Web suffered a brief White Out that wiped many sectors; when it reset, Sleepers had caught up, and the Web was no longer an untouched frontier.

title: Beyond science against magic
summary: How the modern Traditions see science.

claims.text: Many mages once thought the Council stood against science, an idea that came partly from Technocratic propaganda; the Sons of Ether and the spread of technomagic wore it down.
The fall of Horizon removed some anti-scientific Masters and let younger mages bring technomagic forward.
Today's Traditionalists see their ideas as able to live beside science, giving Sleepers' lives meaning beyond Technocratic order; that, not science itself, is the real quarrel.

title: Amalgams under Control
summary: Why Tradition mages still fight the Union.

claims.text: Many amalgams capture, spy on or kill mages under Control's orders, run unethical experiments, silence dissidents and meddle with the press, whatever their own beliefs.
For every amalgam torn over its orders, at least one does them without a qualm; how hard the Union strikes depends on a mage's threat and sway over the Masses.

title: Descent
summary: The Nephandi goal, in two forms.

claims.text: Nephandi seek individual Descent, wearing away the self in service to their masters, and mass Descent, the slow ruin of the Tellurian.
They favor the easy path, feeding nihilism in culture, politics and technology and letting dupes lead themselves to ruin; grand schemes smack of ego, the vice they condemn.
Marauders, by contrast, take Dynamic ideals to excess, living their own paradigm so fully that they deny the rest of reality.
